L3.1.quote: When the players alternately select pieces of a fixed multiset L, Liu Bang first, Liu Bang’s optimal total equals V(L)=1/2(sum L+D(L)). (The optimum is realised by always selecting a currently longest remaining piece.)
L3.1.note: Correctly reduces optimal claiming to the odd-ranked sum and alternating gap.

L3.2.quote: XY aims to realise a refinement whose pieces can be perfectly matched into pairs of equal length except for a single leftover piece of length 1. Such a multiset has D=1.
L3.2.note: Only an unsupported pairing/binary sketch; no universal construction or valid cut-count proof.

L3.3.quote: Liu Bang places his n marks at the cumulative sums... This partitions the unit stick into n+1 intervals of lengths 2^0/S,2^1/S,...,2^n/S.
L3.3.note: Correct construction, but the induction contains explicit missing bounds, virtual/dummy assertions, and reliance on numerical checks.

parsed.notes: The closed form and reduction are correct. Neither universal bound is proved for all n; both central arguments contain acknowledged or evident logical gaps.
